title: Numerically stable softmax and additive log-ratio derivatives
text: softmax score vector \(\boldsymbol{z}\\mathbb{R}^{K}\) evaluated log-sum-exp (LSE) avoid overflow, \[ s_i=\operatorname{softmax}(\boldsymbol{z})_i=\frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_{k}e^{z_k}} =e^{z_i-\operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})}, \qquad \operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})=m+\log\!\sum_{k}e^{z_k-m}, \quad m=\max_k z_k. \tag{1}\] Listing 1: Stable log-sum-exp softmax R Listing 2: Softmax log-sum-exp PyTorch softmax Jacobian difference diagonal rank-one term, \[ \frac{\partial s_i}{\partial z_j}=s_i(\delta_{ij}-s_j), \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{softmax}}=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s}) -\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}. \tag{2}\] matrix also equals Hessian log-sum-exp, \(\nabla^2\operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s}) -\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}\). softmax vector-valued, second derivative third-order tensor \(H_{ijk}=\partial^2 s_i/(\partial z_j\partial z_k)\), \[ H_{ijk}=s_i\bigl[(\delta_{ij}-s_j)(\delta_{ik}-s_k)-s_j(\delta_{jk}-s_k)\bigr], \tag{3}\] , slice slice, rank-one correction \[ \mathbf{H}^{()}=s_i\Bigl[(\boldsymbol{e}_i-\boldsymbol{s}) (\boldsymbol{e}_i-\boldsymbol{s})^{\top} -\bigl(\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s})-\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}\bigr) \Bigr], \tag{4}\] \(\boldsymbol{e}_i\) \(\)-th canonical basis vector. Listing 3 materialises Eq. 2 Eq. 4 \(O(K^2)\) per slice. Listing 3: Softmax Jacobian Hessian tensor R Listing 4: Batched softmax Jacobian Hessian PyTorch
code: log_sum_exp <- function(z) {   m <- max(z)   m + log(sum(exp(z - m))) }  softmax <- function(z) {   exp(z - log_sum_exp(z)) } import torch import torch.nn.functional as F   def softmax(z: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1) -> torch.Tensor:     return F.softmax(z, dim=dim)   def log_sum_exp(z: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1) -> torch.Tensor:     return torch.logsumexp(z, dim=dim) softmax_jacobian <- function(z) {   s <- softmax(z)   diag(s) - tcrossprod(s) }  softmax_hessian <- function(z) {   s <- softmax(z)   k <- length(s)   jac <- diag(s) - tcrossprod(s)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(k, k, k))   for (i in seq_len(k)) {     di <- (seq_len(k) == i) - s # e_i - s     hessian[i, , ] <- s[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)   }   hessian } def softmax_jacobian(z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """z: [..., K] -> [..., K, K]."""     s = softmax(z, dim=-1)     return torch.diag_embed(s) - s.unsqueeze(-1) * s.unsqueeze(-2)   def softmax_hessian(z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """z: [K] -> H[i, j, k] of shape [K, K, K]."""     s = softmax(z, dim=0)     eye = torch.eye(s.numel(), dtype=s.dtype, device=s.device)     diff = eye - s  # (e_i - s) stacked over i     outer = diff.unsqueeze(-1) * diff.unsqueeze(-2)     jac = torch.diag(s) - torch.outer(s, s)     return s[:, None, None] * (outer - jac.unsqueeze(0))

log_p[..., -1:] additive_logistic_jacobian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   (diag(p) - tcrossprod(p))[, -j, drop = FALSE] }  additive_logistic_hessian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   jac <- diag(p) - tcrossprod(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j, j - 1, j - 1))   for (i in seq_len(j)) {     di <- (seq_len(j) == i) - p     slice <- p[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)     hessian[i, , ] <- slice[-j, -j]   }   hessian } def additive_logistic_jacobian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Jacobian [J, J-1]."""     p = additive_logistic(rho)     return (torch.diag(p) - torch.outer(p, p))[:, :-1]   def additive_logistic_hessian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Hessian [J, J-1, J-1]."""     reference = torch.zeros_like(rho[:1])     augmented = torch.cat([rho, reference])     return softmax_hessian(augmented)[:, :-1, :-1] additive_log_ratio_jacobian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   idx <- seq_len(j - 1)   jac <- matrix(0, j - 1, j)   jac[cbind(idx, idx)] <- 1 / p[idx]   jac[, j] <- -1 / p[j]   jac }  additive_log_ratio_hessian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j - 1, j, j))   for (i in seq_len(j - 1)) {     hessian[i, i, i] <- -1 / p[i]^2     hessian[i, j, j] <- 1 / p[j]^2   }   hessian } def additive_log_ratio_jacobian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Jacobian [J-1, J]."""     j = p.numel()     jac = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     jac[idx, idx] = 1.0 / p[:-1]     jac[:, -1] = -1.0 / p[-1]     return jac   def additive_log_ratio_hessian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Hessian [J-1, J, J]."""     j = p.numel()     hessian = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     hessian[idx, idx, idx] = -1.0 / p[:-1].square()     hessian[:, -1, -1] = 1.0 / p[-1].square()     return hessian

code: additive_log_ratio_jacobian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   idx <- seq_len(j - 1)   jac <- matrix(0, j - 1, j)   jac[cbind(idx, idx)] <- 1 / p[idx]   jac[, j] <- -1 / p[j]   jac }  additive_log_ratio_hessian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j - 1, j, j))   for (i in seq_len(j - 1)) {     hessian[i, i, i] <- -1 / p[i]^2     hessian[i, j, j] <- 1 / p[j]^2   }   hessian } def additive_log_ratio_jacobian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Jacobian [J-1, J]."""     j = p.numel()     jac = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     jac[idx, idx] = 1.0 / p[:-1]     jac[:, -1] = -1.0 / p[-1]     return jac   def additive_log_ratio_hessian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Hessian [J-1, J, J]."""     j = p.numel()     hessian = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     hessian[idx, idx, idx] = -1.0 / p[:-1].square()     hessian[:, -1, -1] = 1.0 / p[-1].square()     return hessian

what: Generate mean profiles with a target pairwise cosine — generate_mean_signature_matrix
title: Generate mean profiles with a target pairwise cosine — generate_mean_signature_matrix
text: Builds \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\) blending shared unit direction \(\boldsymbol{u}\) cell-type-private orthogonal marker directions \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\): $$   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}   =   \sqrt{\rho}\,\boldsymbol{u}   +\sqrt{1-\rho}\,\boldsymbol{v}_{j},   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}   =   s\,   \frac{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}}{     \|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}\|_2   }. $$ \(\rho\[0,1]\) target_cosine \(s>0\) mean_scale (default 10, matching nine-scenario simulation grid). private vectors \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) indicator directions partition \(G\) genes (type \(j\) ) \(\ell_2\)-normalised, \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{k}=0\) \(j\neq k\). shared unit \(\boldsymbol{u}\), $$   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot k}   =   \rho   +   \sqrt{\rho(1-\rho)}\,   \bigl(     \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{j}     +     \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{k}   \bigr)   \qquad (j\neq k). $$ column normalisation pairwise cosines \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) therefore track \(\rho\) closely cross terms \(\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) small relative leading \(\rho\) (many genes per block). global scale \(s\) sets column norms (hence Euclidean separation) without changing angles: fixed \(\rho\), \(\|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2 \propto s\). Prefer dialling \(\rho\) second-order precision weights already control interaction strength; keep \(s\) fixed across scenarios compare mean collinearity alone (Aliee Theis 2021) .

title: Simulate bulk mixtures from a Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
text: Draws purified profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_j\sim\mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) independently cell type forms bulk observations linear mixture $$   \boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }   =\boldsymbol{\mu}^{()}\boldsymbol{p}   =\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j\,\boldsymbol{x}_j^{()}, $$ matching article's conditional model \(\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})\sim \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}))\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})= \sum_j p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\). Equivalently, stacking purified draws three-way array \(\mathcal{X}=(x_{gji})\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J\times N}\), bulk matrix mode-2 tensor–vector contraction $$   \boldsymbol{Y}   =\mathcal{X}\times_{2}\boldsymbol{p},   \qquad   y_{gi}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}x_{gji}\,p_{j}   \quad(g=1,\ldots,G;\; =1,\ldots,N), $$ sample recovers matrix–vector product \(\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }=\boldsymbol{X}_{\cdot\cdot }\,\boldsymbol{p}\) \(\boldsymbol{X}_{\cdot\cdot }\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\).
